"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3584: a verb-versus-function-word detector.

Plain-terms summary: this component goes strongly negative on the verb "make" and its
forms (make, makes, made, making), mildly negative on other verbs, and mildly positive on
the infinitive marker "to" and on small function words (prepositions, pronouns, "a", "is").
Everything else (nouns, digits, punctuation) it leaves near zero. Only the current token
is used; the model's context is ignored.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

import wordnet

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MAKE_FORMS = {"make", "makes", "made", "making"}
FUNCTION_WORDS = {" of", " in", " on", " for", " with", " that", " a", " you", " I", " we",
                  " they", " is", " be", " about", " from", " by", " at", " and"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word in MAKE_FORMS:
        value = -2.2
    elif token.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha() and wordnet.parts_of_speech(word) == {"verb"}:
        value = -0.5
    elif token == " to":
        value = 0.3
    elif token in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value = 0.2
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3585 -- the "of" feature.

What it does: it fires on the word "of" and on the same preposition in other
languages ("de", "di", "del" for Romance languages), and by how much depends on
the word just before it:

* "of" after a word that names a part, quantity or measure of the thing before it
  ("number of", "one of", "end of", "top of", "portion of", "most of", "rest of",
  "majority of", "piece of", "percent of") is strongly positive.
* "of" after other nouns or adjectives ("use of", "instance of", "view of",
  "because of") is weakly positive.
* "of" after a comma, a copula ("is of", "was of") or "and" is slightly negative.
* "de" / "di" / "del" are moderately positive, as the Romance "of".
* Every other token is 0.

The program ignores the rest of the context. It is a readable approximation: the
component's real activation also varies with context that a word list cannot see
(a word-by-word lookup on the previous word tops out near 0.56 variance explained).
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# "of" written with or without a leading space, in capitals or after a hyphen.
OF_WORDS = {"of", "-of", "_of"}

# The Romance "of" (decoded with its leading space).
ROMANCE_OF = {" de", " di", " del"}

# Nouns that name a part, a quantity or a measure, so that "X of" is a partitive.
PARTITIVE = set(
    """number amount one part parts member members end top bottom side sides
    front back edge center centre middle piece pieces portion portions all some
    most each many any half rest none both several few much majority minority
    bulk lot lots bit couple pair pairs percent % sum total type types kind kinds
    sort variety set sets series group collection range size length volume level
    degree quarter third scope extent beginning start tip corner interior inside
    subset segment fraction proportion share dozen handful""".split()
)

# Words after which "of" is grammatical glue, not a part-whole link.
GLUE = {",", "was", "is", "be", "are", "were", "and", "but", "or", "as"}

# Nouns and words after which "of" marks an abstract or causal link.
ABSTRACT = set(
    """instance instead because think consist consists capable regardless view
    use lack terms idea importance evidence that those means effect effects""".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in ROMANCE_OF:
        return carry, 4.0
    if token.strip().lower() not in OF_WORDS:
        return carry, 0.0
    # The word before "of", if it is in the same document.
    previous = ""
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if previous in PARTITIVE:
        return carry, 15.0
    if previous in GLUE:
        return carry, -1.5
    if previous in ABSTRACT:
        return carry, 3.0
    return carry, 8.0

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 3586: a diffuse, near-zero output direction.

What it does: this component writes a small signed amount into the residual stream
at almost every token. Its activation is noisy, with no simple trigger: knowing the
token, its class, or its surrounding context explains well under 1% of its variance.
The best simple predictor found is the average activation for each broad kind of
token. Words and sentence-final punctuation sit slightly below zero, CJK characters
and line breaks slightly above, and the first token of each document is essentially
zero.

This program predicts those class averages. It keeps no state.
"""

import regex

# Mean activation for each broad token class, measured on training text.
MEAN_BY_CLASS = {
    "word": -0.043,      # letters, e.g. "the", "Most"
    "end": -0.056,       # sentence-final . ! ? and their closing quotes
    "digit": -0.020,     # numerals
    "punct": -0.020,     # other punctuation (commas, quotes, brackets)
    "space": -0.005,     # spaces, newlines
    "han": 0.011,        # CJK characters
}


def token_class(text):
    if "\n" in text or text.strip() == "":
        return "space"
    if regex.search(r"\p{Han}", text):
        return "han"
    if regex.fullmatch(r"[.!?…]+[\"'”’)]*", text.strip()):
        return "end"
    if regex.search(r"\p{L}", text):
        return "word"
    if regex.search(r"\d", text):
        return "digit"
    return "punct"


READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Position within the document: the first token of a document is ~0.
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, MEAN_BY_CLASS[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Layer-15 MLP down-projection, component 3587: a chat-structure marker detector.

What it does: this component is mostly quiet, but it is strongly negative on the
markup that frames a conversation. The opening markers <|im_start|>, <tool_call>,
<tool_response>, <think> and </think> push it to about -4.5; the closing markers
<|im_end|>, </tool_call> and </tool_response> push it to about -2.7. Elsewhere it sits
near a small baseline of -0.2, higher inside an assistant turn (about +0.4) and lower
inside user or tool-response text (about -0.5).

The program tracks the speaker role of the current turn and whether it is inside a
tool response. Both reset at each new document. Everything else in the component's
activation (a diffuse, context-dependent signal with no simple token concept) is
left at the baseline.
"""

READS = ()

OPEN_MARKERS = {"<|im_start|>", "<tool_call>", "<tool_response>", "<think>", "</think>"}
CLOSE_MARKERS = {"<|im_end|>", "</tool_call>", "</tool_response>"}
OPEN_VALUE = -4.5
CLOSE_VALUE = -2.7
ASSISTANT_VALUE = 0.4
USER_VALUE = -0.5
BASELINE = -0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (role of the current turn, inside a tool response, document label)
    role, in_tool, doc = carry if carry is not None else (None, False, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        role, in_tool = None, False
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<|im_start|>":
        role = tok.strip()
    if tok == "<tool_response>":
        in_tool = True
    elif tok == "</tool_response>":
        in_tool = False

    if tok in OPEN_MARKERS:
        value = OPEN_VALUE
    elif tok in CLOSE_MARKERS:
        value = CLOSE_VALUE
    elif role == "assistant" and not in_tool:
        value = ASSISTANT_VALUE
    elif role == "user" or in_tool:
        value = USER_VALUE
    else:
        value = BASELINE
    return (role, in_tool, doc), float(value)

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3588 (the component's output is this unit's value times about 1.1).

What it responds to: naming and glossing. Its largest negative values sit on the verbs that
introduce an alias ("known", "called", "named", "nicknamed", "termed", "dubbed"), and its
largest positive values come a few tokens later, inside an appositive or gloss that follows a
name ("X (", "X is an", "sold as Ionol (trademark)", "acronym", "the group").

This program writes that down as three rules:
  1. a naming verb itself                         -> -0.6 (its typical value)
  2. a naming or gloss cue within the last 8 tokens -> +0.09 (the typical value there)
  3. anything else                                 -> +0.03 (the typical value)

It predicts the sign of the common cases, but the variance it explains is essentially zero:
token identity, bigrams and simple context windows all leave most of the variance unexplained.
"""

import re

READS = ()

NAME_VERB = re.compile(r"\s?(known|called|named|termed|nicknamed|dubbed|nicknames?)$", re.I)
NAME_CUE = re.compile(
    r"\s?(known|called|named|termed|nicknamed|dubbed|alias|pseudonym|acronym|abbreviation"
    r"|trademark|nicknames?|sold|referred|stands|aka|means|meaning|also|short)$",
    re.I,
)
WINDOW = 8


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the unit's value at the last token of the prefix."""
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    if NAME_VERB.match(tokens[t]):
        return carry, -0.6
    for i in range(t - 1, max(0, t - WINDOW) - 1, -1):
        if docs[i] != docs[t]:
            break
        if NAME_CUE.match(tokens[i]):
            return carry, 0.09
    return carry, 0.03

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3590 (component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3590).

What the component is: its input direction is almost exactly MLP hidden unit 3590 of
layer 15 (weight 0.8 on that unit, the rest spread thin), so its activation is that unit's
value scaled by the norm of its output column. Read through the unembedding, its output
direction promotes words like "action", "actual", "actionable" and suppresses "try",
"attempt", "speculate". That is a property of the output direction only: on text the
activation does not track it (the mean activation before "actions" is +0.02, before
"try"/"attempt" +0.03, against -0.002 overall).

What the data shows: the activation is dense and noise-like. Its standard deviation is
about 0.4 on almost every kind of token, and it hardly depends on token identity, position
in the document, line position, bracket depth or quote state. Token identity, the previous
8 tokens, and the next token each explain about 1% of its variance on held-out rows, or less.
Its large values (|a| > 3, about 0.1% of positions) carry about 10% of the variance, but
no readable rule predicts their sign.

What this program does: it predicts 0 at every position, the best constant for this
measure, since the activation's mean is about 0. It explains about 0% of the variance, and
its effect on the model's next-token predictions is the same as switching the component
off. A token-mean table would add about 2% of variance on held-out rows, at the cost of a
long list of token ids with no concept behind it.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation at this position: zero, since no readable rule predicts it."""
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 3591 (the component is this unit, scaled by about 1.27).

What it responds to, as far as the text shows:
  * It dips negative on the symbols of a mathematical set-up: the words "Let",
    "Suppose", "say", "denote", "Wait" and the "=", "(", ")" and single-letter
    variables that follow them. The dip is deeper while a set-up is still being
    worked out, so the program carries a decaying count of recent set-up words.
  * Everywhere else it sits near zero, with large unpredictable spikes. Most of
    its variance (about 99%) is not captured by any token or context rule tried:
    token identity, the next token, the model's own uncertainty, position,
    repetition and coarse genre all explain almost nothing. Its output direction
    has no readable logit effect. So this program is a weak, honest sketch of
    the negative side of the component, not a full account of it.
The count resets at each new document, as attention does.
"""

import re

READS = ()

DECAY = 0.9
SETUP_WORD = re.compile(
    r"^\s*(Wait|Hmm|Let|let|Suppose|suppose|Assume|assume|say|denote|Denote|"
    r"Maybe|maybe|perhaps|Perhaps|pose)$"
)
SETUP_SYMBOL = re.compile(r"^\s*(=|:=|\)=|\(|\)|[A-Za-z]|\d+)$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    state, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    this_doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if this_doc != doc:
        state = 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    is_word = SETUP_WORD.match(token) is not None
    state = DECAY * state + (1.0 if is_word else 0.0)
    symbol = SETUP_SYMBOL.match(token) is not None
    value = -0.3 * state - 0.3 * state * symbol - 0.35 * is_word
    return (state, this_doc), float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3592: predicted as a constant 0.

What this component does, as far as I could find: nothing a reader can name.
Its activation is a diffuse linear readout of layer 15's MLP hidden state. The
readout is led by hidden unit 3592 but spreads over thousands of other units.
Measured on training text:
- Token identity explains none of its variance (holdout R^2 about 0).
- The previous token adds nothing (R^2 about 0).
- Surface features (space-prefixed, digit, punctuation, newline, non-ASCII,
  position in document) explain about 0.1%.
- The 16 preceding tokens as a bag of words explain about 1%.
- Its output direction, read through the unembedding, promotes and suppresses
  an unrelated scatter of tokens with no common theme.
- Its sign flips about evenly, with a roughly Gaussian spread (std 0.32).
The decomposition agrees it is inert: its causal importance is about 0 everywhere,
and switching it off barely moves the model's predictions.

So the program predicts the component's mean, which is 0 to within noise, at every
position. A conceptual predictor would not do better than this.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # No token, position or context rule carries the signal; predict 0.
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP neuron 3593 (component 3593 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj).

This component is essentially one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP: its input
vector puts 0.79 on that unit (44% of its squared norm), and that unit alone
carries about 56% of the component's variance. The activation is sparse in its
tail and diffuse in its bulk. It fires on the punctuation that opens a value
in structured or quoted text:

- The "of" in a Wikidata-style "X — instance of — Y" triple (strongest, up to ~20).
- The second separator ("—", "|", "->") on a line, the one that sits between a
  property and its value in "Subject — property — value" lists.
- Opening quotation marks that start a quoted phrase in prose, and colons that
  introduce a value ("occupation: ...").

Everything else is near zero. Code, paths and logs are not modelled; the
neuron is slightly negative there, which this program does not capture.

The program tracks, per line, how many triple separators it has seen, and
resets at newlines and at document boundaries.
"""

READS = ()

INSTANCE_OF_VALUE = 12.0  # "of" right after "instance" in a triple
TRIPLE_VALUE = 3.0  # 2nd+ triple separator on the line
OPEN_QUOTE_VALUE = 1.1  # opening quote that starts a quoted phrase
COLON_VALUE = 0.6  # colon introducing a value

TRIPLE_SEPARATORS = {" —", " |", " ->"}
OPEN_QUOTES = {' "', " “", " `", " '", "“"}
COLONS = {":", " :"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    count = 0 if carry is None else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    new_document = (
        len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if new_document or "\n" in prev:
        count = 0

    if token == " of" and prev.strip() == "instance":
        value = INSTANCE_OF_VALUE
    elif token in TRIPLE_SEPARATORS:
        value = TRIPLE_VALUE if count >= 1 else 0.0
        count += 1
    elif token in OPEN_QUOTES:
        value = OPEN_QUOTE_VALUE
    elif token in COLONS:
        value = COLON_VALUE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return count, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 3594: a "courtesy and good-wishes" detector.

What it responds to: stock polite phrases a speaker uses to thank, apologise, wish or
welcome someone ("Thank you", "Thanks for", "I hope", "apologize for", "look forward to",
"good luck", "welcome to"), the courtesy words themselves ("thank", "sorry", "glad",
"congratulations"), and a passage's warm, praising tone, which keeps the response going on
the words that follow. Its activation is strongly negative there,
and near zero on ordinary text.

The program predicts that activation with three rules:
  1. a courtesy formula's second word: about -4;
  2. a courtesy word on its own: about -1.5;
  3. a decaying "warmth" carried from earlier praise or courtesy words in the same
     document, subtracted in proportion (decay 0.9 per token).
Everything else predicts 0. It explains only a small share of the variance: most of the
component's activation is diffuse and context-dependent, and token identity alone explains
under 1%.
"""

READS = ()

FORMULA_GAIN = 4.0
WORD_GAIN = 1.5
STATE_GAIN = 0.5
DECAY = 0.9

COURTESY = {
    "thank", "thanks", "thankful", "appreciate", "appreciated", "appreciation", "gratitude",
    "grateful", "sorry", "apologize", "congratulations", "congrats", "delighted", "proud",
    "honored", "honoured", "hope", "glad", "welcome", "wishing", "wish", "enjoy", "happy",
    "dear",
}
PRAISE = COURTESY | {
    "love", "great", "amazing", "wonderful", "beautiful", "talented", "lovely", "perfect",
    "awesome", "best", "blessed", "excellent", "kind", "good", "pleasure", "honor", "dedicated",
}
FORMULA = {
    ("thank", "you"), ("thanks", "for"), ("thank", "for"), ("hope", "you"), ("i", "hope"),
    ("we", "hope"), ("hope", "this"), ("hope", "that"), ("apologize", "for"), ("sorry", "for"),
    ("i", "apologize"), ("good", "luck"), ("forward", "to"), ("look", "forward"),
    ("looking", "forward"), ("welcome", "to"), ("really", "appreciate"), ("wish", "you"),
    ("glad", "to"), ("happy", "to"), ("honored", "to"), ("honoured", "to"), ("my", "dear"),
    ("you", "all"), ("hard", "work"), ("worked", "hard"), ("thanks", "again"),
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        before = ""
    warmth = 0.0 if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    warmth *= DECAY
    if word in PRAISE:
        warmth += 1.0
    if (before, word) in FORMULA:
        value = -FORMULA_GAIN
    elif word in COURTESY:
        value = -WORD_GAIN
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return warmth, value - STATE_GAIN * warmth

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3595 (read through one component), as a connector detector.

The unit is a weak, noisy feature. It is positive on connecting words that
continue a phrase (prepositions and commas), higher after a verb or adjective than
after a noun: "missed [,] overlooked", "infer [from] the flow chart", "I think [,]".
It is negative on conjunctions that join nouns or adjectives: "willing [and] able",
"some person [or] persons". Everything else sits near zero.

Each value is the mean activation for that (connector kind, previous word kind)
pair, fit on training text. Word kind comes from WordNet: a previous word with a
verb sense counts as a verb, else a noun, else an adjective or adverb.
This explains only about 1% of the variance: the unit's spread within a
connector is much larger than any word-class rule captures.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping
from functools import lru_cache

import wordnet

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

PREPOSITIONS = frozenset(
    "in from by at for into through on with to after over under between within "
    "without about during around against among across like than as of up down out off".split()
)
COMMAS = frozenset(",，、")
CONJUNCTIONS = frozenset("and or but nor".split())

# mean activation by (connector kind, previous word kind)
TABLE = {
    ("preposition", "verb"): 0.36,
    ("preposition", "noun"): -0.10,
    ("preposition", "adjective"): 0.29,
    ("preposition", "other"): 0.20,
    ("comma", "verb"): 0.60,
    ("comma", "noun"): 0.08,
    ("comma", "adjective"): 0.45,
    ("comma", "other"): 0.28,
    ("conjunction", "verb"): 0.23,
    ("conjunction", "noun"): -0.19,
    ("conjunction", "adjective"): -0.29,
    ("conjunction", "other"): -0.05,
}


def connector_kind(token: str) -> str | None:
    """The kind of connector a token is, or None if it is not one."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if token.strip() in COMMAS:
        return "comma"
    if word in PREPOSITIONS:
        return "preposition"
    if word in CONJUNCTIONS:
        return "conjunction"
    return None


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def word_kind(token: str) -> str:
    """The word class of a token, by WordNet: verb, noun, adjective or other."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not word.isalpha():
        return "other"
    senses = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    if "verb" in senses:
        return "verb"
    if "noun" in senses:
        return "noun"
    if "adjective" in senses or "adverb" in senses:
        return "adjective"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """The unit's activation at the newest token: a connector's table value, else 0."""
    kind = connector_kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    same_document = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and (
        prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]
    )
    if kind is None or not same_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = word_kind(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    return carry, float(TABLE[(kind, before)])

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3596 of Qwen3-1.7B, as a readable program.

What the unit does (checked on training rows): it is mostly a digit detector. Digits
are about 9% of tokens but carry about half of the unit's variance. Its gate
pre-activation is positive on roughly a third of digit tokens, and the size of its
output tends to grow over the digits of a multi-digit number. Its sign is set by a
separate up-projection, which is positive about as often as negative on digits. Within
one number the sign is consistent, but it is not predictable from the tokens before it:
not from the digit identity, not from the token before, not from the words a few tokens
back (a bag-of-previous-tokens regression explains under 1% of digit variance).

So a program that sees only tokens cannot say which way the unit pushes on a digit.
Any non-zero guess that ignores the sign makes the prediction worse, so the best
readable prediction is zero everywhere, which is the same as switching the unit off
(eval: variance explained about -0.003, kl_fraction about 0.999).
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3597: a diffuse component with no concept we could name.

Its activation is the hidden unit 3597 of layer 15's MLP (about a quarter of its input weight)
plus many small contributions from the rest of the hidden layer. Its values look like zero-mean noise
(std 0.28, mean 0.024) and are not tied to any token class, position in the document, or
previous token: each explains under 1% of its variance on held-out data.

This program predicts the component's typical value everywhere, its mean, 0.024.
It explains almost none of the variance; a per-token lookup would add about 2%.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.024


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 3598: a weak, mostly unexplained feature.

What it does: its activation is mostly small and noisy (std about 0.39), and it is
hardly set by the current token. This program predicts the activation from the
current token alone, using a few word classes that carry the most signal:

- Agent and source prepositions ("by", "from") and the modular "mod" run negative.
  The strongest case is "mod" (about -1.3), then "by" (about -0.3, most negative
  when it names a legal or formal agent: "enacted by", "approved by").
- Copulas and linking words ("is", "are", "be", "was", "or", "as") run slightly positive.
- Everything else sits at the global mean, about 0.03.

Values are token means from 8192 training rows. The program is not a full
explanation: the token alone explains under 1% of the variance.
"""

READS = ()

BASE = 0.03
TOKEN_VALUE = {
    " mod": -1.3,
    " by": -0.27,
    " from": -0.16,
    " at": -0.06,
    " that": -0.06,
    " not": -0.10,
    " is": 0.12,
    " are": 0.14,
    " be": 0.17,
    " was": 0.07,
    " or": 0.18,
    " as": 0.09,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, TOKEN_VALUE.get(prefix.token_strings[-1], BASE)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3599, read through its down_proj component.

The component's activation is almost exactly this one MLP hidden unit (its
down_proj read vector is ~67% that unit). Across the corpus the activation is
small and diffuse (std ~0.5), but at the end of a reasoning block it is strongly
negative and very consistent: the '</think>' token sits near -9.6.

This program: predict -9.6 on every '</think>' token and 0 everywhere else.
"""

READS = ()

THINK_END = "</think>"
THINK_END_VALUE = -9.6


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.token_strings[prefix.position] == THINK_END:

What it does, in plain terms:
- On <|endoftext|> (the token that ends a document) it is strongly negative,
  about -5 right after a short document and down to about -14 after a long one.
- On the digits of a phone or fax number, e.g. "(213) 3" or "414-9", it is negative
  (about -8 to -10 on the digit that completes the number's usual format).
- Inside LaTeX citation keys (\\cite{...}) it is positive, and so are digits in
  bracketed reference numbers ("[4" "3]") and digits after "et al".
- Everything else predicts 0. Its large variance is spread thinly over many
  tokens, so this program explains only part of it.

document started). Both reset at each document boundary and at <|endoftext|>.

import math
import re

READS = ()

PHONE_PAREN = re.compile(r"\(\d{3}\)\s?\d*$")  # "(213) 3"
PHONE_DASH = re.compile(r"\b\d{3}-\d{3}-\d*$")  # "414-955-1"
PHONE_LOOSE = re.compile(r"(\(\d{3}\)\s?|\b\d{3}-|\b\d{3}\.)\d[\d\-\.\s]{0,12}$")
CITE_KEY = re.compile(r"\\?cite\w*\{[^}]*$")  # inside \cite{...}
CITE_NUM = re.compile(r"\[\d{0,3}$|et al[^\n]{0,15}$")  # "[4", "et al., 2001"
WORD = re.compile(r"\s*[A-Za-z]+")
DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text, n = carry if carry is not None else ("", 0)
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) > 1 and ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        text, n = "", 0  # a new document starts: forget the old one
    x = text + tok
    if tok == END:
        value = max(-15.0, -2.9 - 2.2 * math.log(n + 1))  # longer documents, larger drop
        return ("", 0), float(value)
    value = 0.0
    if DIGIT.fullmatch(tok):
        if PHONE_PAREN.search(x) or PHONE_DASH.search(x):
            value = -9.0
        elif PHONE_LOOSE.search(x):
            value = -2.0
        elif CITE_KEY.search(x) or CITE_NUM.search(x):
            value = 2.0
    elif CITE_KEY.search(x) and WORD.fullmatch(tok):
        value = 6.0
    return (x[-40:], n + 1), float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP output direction 3607 (down_proj of Qwen3-1.7B), in plain terms.

The component reads the MLP's hidden state and writes into the residual stream.
Its activation is large in two opposite situations, both about the current token:

- Negative on opening marks that start a quoted name, an aside or an abbreviation
  in running prose: curly or guillemet quotes, CJK corner brackets, and opening
  parentheses, quotes, backticks, brackets. The strongest cases are an opening
  mark right after a term, where an acronym is about to be defined, as in
  "chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)". Curly, guillemet and corner brackets are the
  most negative; brackets and braces the least.
- Positive on the start of a path or string in code or a tool call: a slash
  opening a file path, `{"` opening a JSON key, `://`, and words such as
  `workspace`, `usr`, `opt`, `tmp`.

Both effects depend on the surrounding text being prose or code. Code-ness is the
share of code punctuation (brackets, slashes, operators) among the characters of
the last 24 tokens of the same document. Opening marks are damped as code-ness
rises (they are near zero in code), and path starts are damped in prose.

Everything else is predicted as zero. Predictions are in the component's
activation units.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

CURLY_OPENERS = {" “", "“", " «", "「", "『", " ‘", "（", " „"}  # mean about -3 in prose
ROUND_OPENERS = {" (", "(", " `", ' "'}  # about -1.5 to -2 in prose
PLAIN_OPENERS = {" [", " {", " '", " $"}  # about -0.7 in prose
PATH_STARTS = {" /", '{"', "://", "workspace", "usr", "opt", "tmp"}  # about +2 to +3.5
CODE_CHARS = set("{}();=<>/\\_[]$#:|*&+-")
WINDOW = 24


def code_share(tokens):
    chars = sum(len(t) for t in tokens)
    return sum(c in CODE_CHARS for t in tokens for c in t) / max(1, chars)


def is_word(token):
    word = token.strip()
    return len(word) >= 2 and word.isascii() and word.isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, ())
    recent = (carry[1] + (tok,))[-WINDOW:]
    carry = (doc, recent)
    code = code_share(recent)
    prose = max(0.1, 1.0 - code / 0.25)  # opening marks fade out in code
    if tok in CURLY_OPENERS:
        value = -3.1 * prose
    elif tok in ROUND_OPENERS:
        after_word = len(recent) > 1 and is_word(recent[-2])
        value = (-2.7 if after_word else -1.2) * prose
    elif tok in PLAIN_OPENERS:
        value = -1.1 * prose
    elif tok in PATH_STARTS:
        value = 3.2 * min(1.0, code / 0.08)  # path starts fade out in prose
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

MLP down-projection. Most of the time its activation is small noise (std about 0.6). Its big
values are negative, and come almost only from the first few tokens of a document:

- A digit as the document's second token is strongly negative: about -21 when the first token
  is whitespace, about -15 after a digit or a sentence end, about -6 after other punctuation,
  about -4 after a word.
- A digit as the third, fourth, or fifth-to-eighth token, with no word yet, is mildly negative
  (about -3, -1.5, and -0.4).
- Other non-word tokens at position 1 (whitespace, punctuation) are mildly negative, about
  -2 to -4.5, and ordinary words about -0.8.
- An ellipsis is about -1.4, and the diff hunk marker "@@" about -9.

Everything else is predicted as 0. The program tracks each token's position in its document
and whether an ordinary word (two or more ASCII letters) has occurred yet, starting over where
the document label changes, as the model does.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

DIGIT = re.compile(r"[0-9]")
WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]{2,}")
SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"[.!?。]")
ELLIPSIS = re.compile(r"\s*\.{2,}\s*")


def first_token_value(text: str) -> float:
    """How strongly a digit right after this first token of a document is negative."""
    if text.strip() == "":
        return -21.0
    if DIGIT.fullmatch(text):
        return -15.0
    if SENTENCE_END.search(text):
        return -14.0
    if WORD.search(text):
        return -4.0
    return -6.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        pos, words = 0, False
    else:
        pos, words = carry[0] + 1, carry[1]
    value = 0.0
    if pos == 1 and DIGIT.fullmatch(tok):
        value = first_token_value(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    elif not words:
        if DIGIT.fullmatch(tok):
            value = {2: -3.0, 3: -1.5}.get(pos, -0.4 if pos < 8 else 0.0)
        elif pos == 1:
            value = -0.8 if WORD.search(tok) else -2.0
    if ELLIPSIS.fullmatch(tok) and pos > 0:
        value = -1.4
    if tok.strip() == "@@":
        value = -9.0
    words = words or bool(WORD.search(tok))
    return (pos, words), value

"""Predicts the activation of layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3636 from document position and token type.

This component is a diffuse, weak direction in the layer-15 MLP output. Its activation is nearly unrelated
to which token is present (token identity explains about 2% of its variance, held out) and to any simple word
class, so no short rule captures most of it. Two things do show up consistently:

- Start of document: the first token of a document reads about 0, the next few tokens read slightly positive,
  and from about the eighth token on it sits at a small negative level.
- Digits and line breaks sit a little lower than other tokens.

The program predicts those means and nothing more.
"""

READS = ()

BASE = -0.066  # typical activation deep inside a document, on ordinary tokens
LOW = -0.115  # typical activation on tokens that contain a digit or a line break
EARLY = {1: 0.16, 2: 0.07, 3: 0.04}  # position in document -> mean activation for the first few tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0  # first token of a document (or of the row)
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if pos == 0:
        value = 0.0
    elif pos in EARLY:
        value = EARLY[pos]
    elif any(c.isdigit() for c in token) or "\n" in token:
        value = LOW
    else:
        value = BASE
    return (doc, pos), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 3637: a weak, noise-like readout with no readable trigger.

What it is: the component reads the layer-15 MLP hidden vector through one direction V_c.
That direction is dominated by hidden unit 3637 (weight 0.43 of norm 0.82), with many small
weights on the other units. Its activation is roughly Gaussian: mean 0.02, std 0.32, and it
is only weakly autocorrelated from token to token. It is not explained by the current token,
the previous few tokens, the position in a document, sentence or line boundaries, or repeats:
held-out fits on those features give variance explained of about zero. Its causal importance
is essentially zero, so it hardly moves the model's output.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value, 0.02, at every token, and
0 at each document's first token, where the activation is always near zero. It explains almost
none of the variance. It is the honest baseline, not a mechanism.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_VALUE = 0.02  # the component's mean activation over the eval-like rows


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A document starts where the document label changes, or at the row's first token.
    first = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return None, 0.0 if first else MEAN_VALUE

"""Year-ending digit detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3638.

What the component does: it is almost silent everywhere, but when the model reads
the last digit of a four-digit year it pushes strongly negative. The strongest
cases are years in 2000-2029 (e.g. the "8" of "2018"), then 1500-1999 (weaker).
The program predicts that: a negative value on the fourth digit of a standalone
four-digit number whose first three digits are "20x" (-2.0) or "15x"-"19x" (-1.3),
and 0 everywhere else.

What it does not capture: the component also has a small, diffuse signal on
ordinary tokens (std about 0.3 over all tokens) that has no simple concept behind
it here. This program explains only the large, concentrated negative spikes.
"""

READS = ()


def _is_digit(s):
    return len(s) == 1 and s.isdigit()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    if t < 3:
        return carry, 0.0
    # The last four tokens must be digits from one document, and the number must
    # start here (no digit before it), so this is the fourth digit of a 4-digit number.
    if not all(_is_digit(s) for s in toks[t - 3 : t + 1]):
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(set(docs[t - 3 : t + 1])) > 1:
        return carry, 0.0
    if t >= 4 and _is_digit(toks[t - 4]):
        return carry, 0.0
    head = toks[t - 3] + toks[t - 2]  # first two digits of the number
    if head == "20":
        return carry, -2.0
    if head[0] == "1" and head[1] in "56789":
        return carry, -1.3
    return carry, 0.0

"""Closing brackets that end an aside: this component is large but sign-unstable there.

What it does: on the ')' or ']' that closes a parenthetical or bracketed aside, such as
"(Figure 2A)", "(released June 1994)" or "[13]", the component's activation is large in
size (typically 1 to 10, sometimes over 15) and about as often positive as negative (58%
positive). Elsewhere it is near zero, with a small spread. Tokens right after a closer are
somewhat more spread than other tokens.

What this program predicts: only the average level. Each closing bracket gets 0.6 for the
first two closers in its document and 0.2 after that; every other token gets 0. It has
no sign information, so it explains almost no variance. Surface cues we tested (the token
before the bracket, digits or CJK in the aside, the aside's length, the position in the
document) did not predict the sign.
"""

READS = ()

CLOSERS = ")]）"  # ASCII ')' and ']' and the full-width ')'


def is_closer(token):
    """True if the token starts with a closing bracket, e.g. ')', '),', ']\\n'."""
    head = token.lstrip()[:1]
    return head != "" and head in CLOSERS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    count, doc = carry if carry is not None else (0, None)
    doc_now = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc_now != doc:
        count = 0  # a new document: the count of earlier closers restarts
    value = 0.0
    if is_closer(prefix.token_strings[-1]):
        value = 0.6 if count < 2 else 0.2
        count += 1
    return (count, doc_now), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 3640: a weak, diffuse readout of the MLP's hidden state.

What it is: the component reads the layer-15 MLP hidden vector through one direction
(V column 3640, about 0.25 on hidden unit 3640 and smaller weights on many others) and
writes along one residual direction (U row 3640, norm 0.75). Its causal importance is
essentially zero everywhere, and zeroing it barely moves the output.

What this program does: it has no token- or topic-level concept that explains the
activation (token identity, WordNet categories and a hand lexicon all leave R^2 near 0).
The only regularity found is a weak dependence on position in the document: it is
slightly positive over the first few dozen tokens of a document and close to zero
afterwards. So the program predicts that profile, a document-position average.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation by position within a document (token index k, 0 = first token).
EARLY = 0.065   # k = 2..15
MID = 0.03      # k = 16..63
LATE = 0.008    # k >= 64


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        k = 0
    else:
        k = carry[1] + 1
    if k < 2:
        value = 0.0
    elif k < 16:
        value = EARLY
    elif k < 64:
        value = MID
    else:
        value = LATE
    return (doc, k), value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3641 (the component's whole input direction is this one unit).

It is silent on nearly every token. Its large values come from numeric ranges written as
lists, such as "8910..8939 , 8940..8969 , 8970..8999":
  * On the last digit "9" of the upper end of a range "A..B", when B has as many digits as A
    (the number is at least MIN_DIGITS long), it is strongly positive (about +57).
  * On the "0" that ends a long number followed by " ," (the start of the next range, which
    is then followed by ".."), it is negative (about -14).
Other digits, and all other tokens, are predicted as 0. The rest of its variance is spread
over many weak, varied contexts (digits in decimals, comma-grouped numbers, etc.) that a
short rule does not capture.

The program reads only the current number and the tokens just before it, within the same
document, so it carries no state between positions.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = frozenset("0123456789")
MIN_DIGITS = 4      # shorter numbers do not fire
RANGE_END = 57.0    # "9" closing the upper end "B" of "A..B", with B as long as A
RANGE_START = -14.0 # "0" closing a long number followed by " ," (a list item before "..")


def _digits_before(strings, docs, end):
    """How many digits end at index `end` (inclusive) in the same document."""
    i = end
    while i >= 0 and strings[i] in DIGITS and docs[i] == docs[end]:
        i -= 1
    return end - i


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s, d, t = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids, prefix.position
    if s[t] not in DIGITS:
        return carry, 0.0
    n = _digits_before(s, d, t)  # digits of this number so far, including this one
    if n < MIN_DIGITS:
        return carry, 0.0
    j = t - n                    # token before the number
    while j >= 0 and s[j] == " " and d[j] == d[t]:  # skip spaces
        j -= 1
    if j < 0 or d[j] != d[t]:
        return carry, 0.0
    if s[t] == "9" and s[j] == "..":
        if _digits_before(s, d, j - 1) == n:  # the start "A" had as many digits
            return carry, RANGE_END
    if s[t] == "0" and s[j] == " ,":
        return carry, RANGE_START
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 3643, as the component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3643.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's down_proj. Its read direction V_c is
about 68% the single MLP hidden unit 3643 (the unit's own value, silu(gate) * up), so its
activation is roughly that unit's value times 1.06. It writes a small amount into the
residual stream.

What this program does: it predicts the component's mean activation (about 0.04) at every
position, and the first token of each document predicts 0 (the unit is near zero there). No
simple rule about the token, its neighbours, its position in the document, repetition, or
copying explained the rest. Lexical bag-of-context features reached only about 1% of the
variance on held-out text, so the program is a baseline, not an explanation of the
activation's sign or size.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0378  # the component's mean over eval-like text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Predict the activation at the newest position of the packed row."""
    t = prefix.position
    starts_document = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 3644 (this component is that one hidden unit, rescaled).

It is quiet almost everywhere and spikes, in either direction and up to |50|, inside
identifier-like text: case and patent numbers, DOIs, URLs, section and figure references.
Inside such text a digit that starts a number is pushed negative, a digit that continues
a number is pushed positive, and letters and punctuation are pushed negative. Elsewhere
it sits near zero.

The spikes' sign and size are not predictable from the text by these rules: this program
predicts only the average value of each group, so it captures very little of the variance.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Markers of identifier-like citation text (case, patent, DOI, URL, section, figure).
MARKERS = re.compile(
    rb"Patent|Application|Docket|Unit |Case|cv|No\.|No |Ser\.|\xc2\xa7|Section|"
    rb"doi|DOI|pone|https?://|arXiv|ISBN|#"
)
# Average activation of each group, measured on training rows.
STARTS_NUMBER = -0.58  # digit that starts a number, inside identifier text
CONTINUES_NUMBER = 0.15  # digit after a digit, inside identifier text
OTHER_IN_IDENTIFIER = -0.20  # letters or punctuation inside identifier text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: (recent bytes of this document, whether the previous token was a digit)."""
    window, prev_digit = carry if carry is not None else (b"", False)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[max(len(prefix.document_ids) - 2, 0)]:
        window, prev_digit = b"", False
    token = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    window = (window + token)[-48:]
    is_digit = token.strip().isdigit()
    value = 0.0
    if MARKERS.search(window):
        if is_digit:
            value = CONTINUES_NUMBER if prev_digit else STARTS_NUMBER
        elif token.strip():
            value = OTHER_IN_IDENTIFIER
    return (window, is_digit), value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 3645 (this component is almost exactly that unit).

A caution detector. The unit is positive while the text is declining, apologising, or
flagging something as inappropriate, private, sensitive, illegal or unsafe ("I'm sorry, but I
cannot", "an invasion of privacy", "inappropriate content"). It stays positive for a few
words afterwards, fading over about eight tokens, and it stays raised through an assistant
reply that opens with a refusal or apology. Everywhere else it sits near its typical value.
"""

READS = ()

# Words of refusal, apology, and sensitivity, propriety or legality.
CAUTION = {
    "sorry", "apologize", "apologise", "cannot", "unable", "refuse", "decline",
    "inappropriate", "appropriate", "offensive", "harmful", "harm", "illegal",
    "unethical", "ethical", "moral", "privacy", "private", "sensitive", "sensitivity",
    "concern", "concerned", "concerns", "consent", "safety", "safe", "unsafe", "risk",
    "dangerous", "explicit", "sexual", "violence", "responsible", "responsibility",
    "policy", "guidelines", "controversial", "controversy", "taboo", "censor",
    "permission", "allowed", "acceptable", "unacceptable", "confidential", "secret",
    "comfortable",
}
# Words that open a refusal when they appear early in an assistant reply.
OPENERS = {
    "sorry", "apologize", "apologise", "cannot", "unable", "refuse", "decline",
    "unethical", "inappropriate", "illegal", "harmful",
}

DECAY = 0.85  # per token: the caution level fades over about eight tokens
GAIN = 0.45  # predicted activation per unit of caution level
REPLY = 0.7  # extra predicted activation inside a reply that opens with a refusal
BASE = 0.07  # the unit's typical value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower().strip(".,!?'\"")
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        carry = {"level": 0.0, "role": None, "pending": False, "count": 0, "refusal": False}
    s = dict(carry)
    # Track chat turns: <|im_start|> then the role name, until <|im_end|>.
    if prefix.token_strings[-1] == "<|im_start|>":
        s["pending"], s["role"] = True, None
    elif s["pending"]:
        s["pending"], s["role"] = False, word
        s["count"], s["refusal"] = 0, False
    elif prefix.token_strings[-1] == "<|im_end|>":
        s["role"] = None
    # Inside an assistant reply, see whether it opens with a refusal.
    if s["role"] == "assistant":
        s["count"] += 1
        if s["count"] <= 12 and word in OPENERS:
            s["refusal"] = True
    s["level"] = s["level"] * DECAY + (1.0 if word in CAUTION else 0.0)
    in_refusal_reply = s["refusal"] and s["role"] == "assistant"
    value = BASE + GAIN * s["level"] + (REPLY if in_refusal_reply else 0.0)
    return s, value

"""Purpose / use detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3646.

What the component is: essentially MLP hidden unit 15.3646 (about 44% of its variance).
Its activation is mostly near zero with a diffuse spread, but it dips strongly negative
where the text is about what something is used for, intended for, or allocated to.
Switched on in that region, its output pushes the next-word guess toward "use / usage /
utilize / purpose" words.

What this program does: it predicts a negative value on
  1. words about use or purpose ("use", "used", "usage", "purpose", "intended", "serve"...);
  2. words about plans, allocation or consumption ("aim", "plans", "reserved", "spent",
     "sold", "proceeds", "mainly", ...), slightly weaker;
  3. short function words ("to", "for", "be", "may", "can", "will", "and", "is"...)
     that come within two tokens after a word of either kind, e.g. "used [for]",
     "intended [to]", "may [be]".
Everything else is predicted as 0.

Honest limits: this captures very little of the variance. The sparse purpose-word
firing is only about a fifth of the total variance even for a perfect oracle, and
simple word rules recover well under 1% of it. The diffuse bulk is not captured.
Switching the component off, or this program, moves the model's output almost equally.
"""

READS = ()

# Words about using or having a purpose.
USE_WORDS = {
    "use", "uses", "used", "using", "usage", "utilize", "utilized", "utilise",
    "utilization", "purpose", "purposes", "intention", "intended", "serve", "serves",
    "serving", "unused",
}

# Words about plans, allocation, spending or consumption.
ALLOT_WORDS = {
    "aim", "aims", "plan", "plans", "planned", "meant", "designed", "reserved",
    "allocated", "allocation", "invested", "spent", "consumed", "consume", "sold",
    "distributed", "divided", "proceeds", "waste", "benefit", "benefits", "applications",
    "application", "dedicated", "devoted", "primarily", "mainly", "mostly", "solely",
    "largely",
}

# Short function words that take a purpose after them ("used [for]", "may [be]").
FOLLOWERS = {"to", "for", "be", "may", "can", "will", "and", "was", "is", "were", "are"}

USE_VALUE = -0.5
ALLOT_VALUE = -0.6
FOLLOW_VALUE = -0.3


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    if word in USE_WORDS:
        return carry, USE_VALUE
    if word in ALLOT_WORDS:
        return carry, ALLOT_VALUE
    if word in FOLLOWERS:
        # Look at the two tokens before this one, within the same document.
        ids = prefix.document_ids
        for k in (2, 3):
            if len(ids) >= k and ids[-k] == ids[-1]:
                if _word(prefix.token_strings[-k]) in USE_WORDS | ALLOT_WORDS:
                    return carry, FOLLOW_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Negative on words of revision: a fix, a bug, a mistake, a doubt or a "but".

Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3647 writes along a direction whose negative side promotes
correction words ("correction", "bug", "corrected"). Its activation is strongly negative where
the text is revising itself or a piece of work: "typo", "fix", "bug", "mistake", "issue",
"wrong", "Actually", "Wait", "But", "maybe". It is near zero elsewhere.

This program predicts -0.9 on such a word, -0.2 for the 8 tokens after one (the revision
mode lingers a little), and 0 otherwise. Counting restarts at each document. It explains
about 1% of the activation's variance: most of the component is a diffuse signal that no
short word list captures.
"""

READS = ()

REVISION = set(
    "fix fixes fixed fixing bug bugs typo typos mistake mistakes mistaken error errors "
    "issue issues wrong incorrect incorrectly correct correction corrected misunderstanding "
    "problem problems confusing misleading deprecated ambiguous unclear flawed broken "
    "actually wait but however maybe perhaps although though hmm instead".split()
)
ON, NEAR, LINGER = -0.9, 8, -0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # tokens since the last revision word (carry is that count at the previous position)
    gap = 99 if carry is None or new_doc else carry + 1
    if word in REVISION:
        return 0, ON
    return gap, (LINGER if gap <= NEAR else 0.0)
